exposure: antenatal imaging characteristics (polyhydramnios, tracheal deviation and compression, anterior mass location, antenatally-estimated mass volume)
outcome: invasive airway management at birth (endotracheal intubation, tracheostomy)
postnatal cervical mass management (surgical excision, sclerotherapy, adjuvant therapy with rapamycin)
cohort: The study included 52 patients with antenatally diagnosed neck masses from a single center between January 2008 and January 2019.
finding: Polyhydramnios, tracheal deviation and compression, anterior mass location, and increasing antenatally-estimated mass volume were significantly associated with invasive airway intervention at birth, EXIT procedure, and tracheostomy during neonatal hospitalization.
gest_age: Mean gestational age at time of diagnostic imaging was 29 weeks 3 days (range: 19w4d - 37w).
